excerpt: Paradise Metal is a sleight of hand. The music within has very little to do with metal in the conventional sense, and everything to do with the genre's outer limits—the kind of undulating drone movements practiced by Earth and SUNN O))). Father Dionysios Tabakis is an Orthodox priest serving at the Church of the Panagitsa in Nafplio, Greece. Instruments include the ney, oud, and lyra. The album is a kind of ancient trance music that addresses age-old maladies: depression, alienation, and isolation.

Los Angeles duo Soltera & Sonido Sex deliver an uncompromising album that transforms pummeling punk, techno, and drum & bass into convulsive catharsis—a celebration of the unburdening powers of the dance floor. Soltera (Tania Ordoñez) is Colombian-American, co-founder of Casa/Teca label. Sonido Sex (Aarum Altorre) is also known as Pacoima Techno and Sylmar Soundsystem. Rooted in queer and Latine experience and womanhood, the album frames the dance floor as a space for purging sorrows through sweat and temporary amnesia.

album: Escape From New York: The Hudson Valley Scene
excerpt: An exploration of why musicians migrate from NYC to the Hudson Valley and the current state of the region's music scene. Features musicians including Jack DeJohnette, Larry Grenadier, John Medeski & John Scofield (album Hudson), Tony Levin (Bringing It Down to the Bass), Rebecca Martin (The Upstate Project), Buke and Gase and Sō Percussion (A Record Of), The Felice Brothers (Valley of Abandoned Songs), and Chris Corsano (The Key). No single Hudson Valley style—spans many genres with a relaxed mood and naturalistic calm.

album: Fifteen Years of Hands In The Dark's Beautiful Lucid Dreaming
excerpt: Hands In The Dark is a French DIY record label approaching its 15th anniversary with nearly 100 releases. The label explores a sound somewhere between ambient, kosmische, electroacoustic music, and free improvisation. Founded by Morgan Cuinet (Ornans, France) and Onito (now Canterbury, England), who met in Besançon. Tom Relleen of The Oscillation became an unofficial third member until his death in 2020. Notable releases include Tomaga's Intimate Immensity and Brian Case, Valby Vokalgruppe, Razen, Piotr Kurek, Selvhenter. The label runs as a non-profit organization.

album: Lost in the Signal: Radio as Instrument
excerpt: An exploration of radio as musical instrument in composition history, featuring John Cage's Imaginary Landscape No. 4 (1951) for 24 performers operating 12 radios, Karlheinz Stockhausen's Kurzwellen (1968) using shortwave radio, and Tod Dockstader's Aerial (1988-2003). Includes interview with Scanner (Robin Rimbaud) on why radio remains compelling: 'Radio remains compelling for me precisely because it resists control.' Discusses radio's unique quality of shared temporal experience.
